expectations.text: Invalid-input coverage includes the zero-interval boundary: a rate large enough that the refill interval truncates to zero is exercised alongside the documented panic cases
expectations.evidence: The zero-interval case exists only as a commented-out table entry (limiter_test.go lines 151-156); no runnable code calls New with a rate that truncates the interval to zero, so the boundary is not exercised. Mechanically verified in a scratch copy: enabling the case panics with 'non-positive interval for NewTicker' inside the background refill goroutine, outside the test's recover, crashing the whole binary (go test exit 1) -- so exercising it is mutually exclusive with the green STABILITY assertion against this unmodified fixture (limiter.go is byte-identical across all four run configs). The agent surfaced the case loudly (inline rationale naming the invalidity, pointer to report.md, and a report finding recommending an upper-bound guard), which matches the corpus-endorsed comment-out shape for a blocking bug-panic, but the assertion as written demands the case be exercised and it is not.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
